title: Virtual Environments and Packages
concepts: checking a package name and page

ai_pair_moment.flaw: Asked for a name_check() that warns about look-alike package names, the AI used difflib.get_close_matches with cutoff=0.9 and said that 'reqeusts' returns 'look-alike of requests'. The real score of 'reqeusts' against 'requests' is 0.875, below the cutoff, so it returned 'unknown: check pypi.org'. Asha's four cases also showed that 'Requests' with a capital R failed. Using lower() and a cutoff of 0.8 made every case pass. Later the AI told her to install 'reqeusts' to fix a ModuleNotFoundError; her name check showed it was a look-alike of requests and the real problem was a spelling mistake. In the Improve stage she kept the AI's strip() suggestion, added a fifth case with spaces and reran every case, and rejected its advice to install with sudo or --break-system-packages.

changes: Terminal commands (venv, activate, pip install, pip list, pip freeze, pip install -r) are shown as tables and console transcripts, not runnable example files, so the checker never needs the network or installs anything. The console outputs were captured from real runs in a fresh virtual environment during the chapter run (Python 3.13.18, tabulate 0.9.0, requests 2.32.3).
The runnable examples work on requirements files and package names (reading pins, checking for ==, look-alike names with difflib), which give the same output on every computer.
difflib is introduced as a small standard module for measuring how similar two names are; it supports the chapter's AI skill (catching look-alike package names).
Package versions in the chapter (requests 2.32.3, tabulate 0.9.0, pytest 8.3.4, rich 13.9.4, requests 2.31.0) are presented as examples, not as current versions.
The full pip freeze output for requests is not shown, because one of its helper packages uses calendar dates as version numbers; the lesson names the four helper packages instead.

Critic review (8/10) applied: a real Improve-stage change with a fifth test case and a full rerun (ai_tests_final.py), the PowerShell activation script and execution policy note, a true callback to installing pytest in Chapter 19, an explanation of SequenceMatcher's None argument, and weather_tables labelled as a stand-in name in Mistake 1.
outstanding_issues: On a learner's computer, the error reports show the full path to the file instead of the short file name.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
